transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Another one at the threshold. They always clear their throats the same way. Speak if you must.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Peace be upon you. I’ve come to ask passage beyond the gate, to find my brother Omar and bring him home.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Home. That word survives the fall more often than names do. Hold on, this coin is scratched.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He was taken by the well, and I followed because I couldn’t leave him alone. I don’t want anything else.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: They never do at first. Rubies chip when you stack them carelessly.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: If there is a rule or a price, I will try to meet it. I just need to reach what lies beyond.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Rules are a human comfort. Prices are for markets, not doors. This one rings dull, hear that.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I understand. I only meant that I am willing to give whatever I can.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Willing is light as dust down here. Everyone arrives full of it. The dust settles; the wanting changes.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then tell me what remains when it settles, and I will try to be that.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You try so neatly. Neat things fray fast in the dark. Hm, this chain was once part of a crown.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don’t know how else to speak. I only know why I came.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Why is a heavy question for such thin air. You bring it like a bowl with a crack.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Because he is my brother, and I was the one who dared him. I think that makes me responsible.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Responsibility rusts faster than iron. I can smell it on you already.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: If it rusts, then I will keep walking until it breaks. I can’t turn back.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Everyone says that before the echoes teach them otherwise. This gem is false, see how the light dies.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then let the echoes teach me too. I only ask that I reach him first.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Asking persists even when it grows hoarse. I have heard that tone split stones thinner than this vein.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don’t know another way to speak to you. I thought if I kept telling the truth, it might matter.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Truth is common as gravel; it crunches under everything. Hold—this filigree bends, it should not.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then I will keep standing until something else is left of me. I don’t have a better offer.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Standing is easy before time leans on you. This gold is too soft; someone mixed fear into it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Fear is all I brought with me, so that sounds right. I can’t set it down.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You say that as if fear were a burden instead of a companion. It follows all of you here, though most pretend otherwise. Continue.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: When I followed him down, my legs were shaking so hard I thought the well would spit me back out. I was more afraid of living without him than of whatever waited below.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: That is not the fear they usually bring. They clutch at pain, or pride, or the hope of being special. This is different.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don’t think I am special. I just keep seeing his back as he fell, and I don’t want that to be the last thing I know of him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Most memories thin quickly once the dark starts teaching. Faces blur, voices flatten, love turns into a shape without a name. You speak as if you are trying to hold one moment still.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I am. If I lose that, then I don’t know why I’m still walking.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Stillness is a strange hunger. Most beg to forget, and you beg to keep. Say more about that moment you are holding, and do not dress it up.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He laughed just before he shouted at the well, and it sounded forced, like he was trying to be brave for me. I remember thinking I should stop him, and I didn’t.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Regret usually comes screaming; yours seems to whisper and sit down. It stays, does it not. What does it ask of you when you are quiet.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It asks me to go where he went, even if I am afraid. It doesn’t tell me what happens after.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: No, it never does. That is how it keeps its teeth clean. Continue, Salim of the surface.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: If I find him and he doesn’t remember me, I think I will still stay. I don’t know how to leave him twice.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: That is an answer shaped like a wound, not a bargain. I did not mean to ask this, but I will: if he forgets you, would you let him.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Yes. If that keeps him alive, I would let him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: How obedient you make yourself sound, as if this were humility and not terror wearing clean clothes. Say it again without pleasing me—would you truly accept being nothing to him.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don’t want to be nothing to him, but I don’t want him gone more. That’s all I know.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Enough. I have stopped counting what shines, and now I am looking at what does not. Tell me one thing you have never said aloud about him.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I was jealous of how easily he laughed, and I loved him for it at the same time.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Jealousy braided with love is not a confession they bring me; they choose one mask and starve the other. That sound you name—easy laughter—did you ever wish it would break so you could hold him instead.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Yes. I hated myself for that thought, and it came anyway.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: There it is. Do not apologize; that would cheapen it, and I have had enough soft metal today. Say what you would have done if it had broken.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I would have stood in front of him and taken the shouting, so he could laugh again later.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: I am listening now. That wanting—to shield the laugh rather than own it—tell me whose need it truly was.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Mine. I needed him to be himself so I could be his brother.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Mine as well, once. I will not ask you to understand that. The gate is open.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then I will go now. Thank you for listening.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Do not thank me. I did this because I wanted to feel something move, and you managed it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I won’t forget why you let me pass.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Go, before I remember something else and change nothing.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I’m going.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You move quickly for someone who says goodbye so carefully. The gate does not close behind you out of mercy; it closes because it is finished listening. Go.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: If I find him, I’ll tell him he laughed well. Even if he doesn’t know why.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: That is not for him, and you know it. It is for the part of you that would follow even if there were no brother at the end. Pass.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: No, you do not, and that is why this works. Go now.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I will go now, then. I hope he remembers how to laugh.
